extracted.intended_audience: clinical researchers, instrument developers, and clinicians interested in measurement reliability and validation of assessment tools
extracted.subtask_description: Identify and apply criteria to assess the reliability, precision, and validity of clinical measurement tools, scoring systems, and classification/grading instruments (inter- and intra-rater agreement, diagnostic accuracy, measurement error, and instrument validity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Intrarater reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Consistency of measurements when the same assessor repeats the measurement (within-session or across sessions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessed via ICC (e.g., ICC3,1) or kappa for categorical data; report 95% CIs. Averaging multiple trials (eg, average of 3 trials) typically increases intrarater reliability; novice and experienced raters can both achieve high intrarater reliability with appropriate technique and training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interrater reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Agreement among different raters assessing the same subjects or images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessed via ICC (eg, ICC2,1 or ICC2,3), Cohen's κ, or weighted κ; report 95% CIs. Reliability can be improved by removing problematic items, clarifying definitions, training raters, or modifying classification elements that show low agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intraclass Correlation Coefficient (ICC) usage and interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of ICC to quantify reliability for continuous/interval measurements, specifying model (eg, two-way mixed, two-way random) and unit (single vs average measures).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report ICC value with 95% CI and state the model used. Common interpretive thresholds cited: ICC > 0.75 = excellent; 0.40–0.75 = fair to good; ICC < 0.40 = poor. Choose appropriate ICC model for study design (eg, two-way mixed absolute agreement for fixed raters).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cohen's kappa and weighted kappa for categorical agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of κ statistics to assess agreement for categorical or ordinal ratings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report κ with 95% CI; use weighted κ for ordinal scales. Interpret values in context (examples in the page show κ values used to judge agreement between learners and experts and to assess intrarater agreement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard error of measurement (SEM) and smallest detectable difference (SDD)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quantify the measurement's inherent error and the minimal change that can be interpreted as real beyond measurement error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report SEM and SDD alongside ICC to describe absolute measurement error; low SEM indicates low measurement error. Use these metrics to judge practical significance of changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precision versus accuracy of landmarks or measurements
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of both repeatability (precision) and closeness to true/reference value (accuracy) for chosen landmarks or measurement protocols.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess via intrarater/interrater ICCs, mean error difference, and confidence intervals. Prefer landmarks/protocols with high precision and accuracy (eg, bilateral mental and infraorbital foramina, anterior nasal spine, nasion) and avoid landmarks with high mean errors (eg, subspinale, lingulae).

rubrics_metrics.name: Concurrent/criterion validity
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree to which a measurement correlates with an accepted reference or criterion (eg, objective instruments vs modified Vancouver Scar Scale).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report correlation coefficients and significance; compute sensitivity and specificity when a categorical reference standard is available. Significant correlations confirm tools measure same trait as reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construct and content validity
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence that the tool measures the intended construct and that its items adequately cover the domain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess via expert consensus (eg, Delphi), comparisons across known groups (shows sensitivity to expertise levels), and statistical analyses (eg, principal component analysis to support dimensionality).

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal consistency (Cronbach's alpha)
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree items within a tool cohere to measure the same construct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report Cronbach's alpha; high values (eg, ≥0.9 in RESCAPE tools) support internal consistency. Interpret in the context of unidimensionality analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dimensionality assessment (principal component analysis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use PCA or similar methods to determine whether the tool is unidimensional or multi-dimensional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unidimensionality supports summing item scores; report PCA results and factor structure to justify score interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diagnostic accuracy (sensitivity, specificity, overall accuracy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability of a test or assessment to correctly identify disease or condition presence/absence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report sensitivity, specificity, accuracy with 95% CIs and compare to reference standard. Discuss limitations (moderate specificity or sensitivity may warrant cautious interpretation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Bias and random error analysis (Bland-Altman)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of systematic bias and limits of agreement between methods or raters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Bland-Altman plots and report limits of agreement and 95% CIs to characterize bias and random error; this complements ICC by showing magnitude and direction of discrepancies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting of mean error differences and confidence intervals
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide mean measurement differences and their uncertainty to evaluate accuracy and precision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include mean error difference, 95% CIs for errors, and discuss clinical relevance of observed differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensitivity to change (responsiveness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tool's ability to detect meaningful changes over time (eg, improvement with training or rehabilitation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate via longitudinal increases/decreases in scores with statistical significance across expertise levels or over training programs; include effect sizes or median score changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and application of acceptable reliability thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-specification or justification of what constitutes acceptable reliability for a given context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different studies cite thresholds (eg, ICC > 0.75 = excellent). Explicitly state thresholds used for interpretation and consider context (clinical vs research use).

rubrics_metrics.name: Feasibility, usability, and workflow considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical aspects such as time to complete, remote applicability, data security, and ease of adoption (eg, iPhone teleradiology feasibility).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess time-to-interpret, platform security (eg, no patient data stored on device), and compare interpretation times to standard workstations; include interrater agreement in feasibility evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for clear administration manuals and rater instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Need for detailed, illustrated manuals to ensure homogeneous application of scales across raters and contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translation/adaptation should add photos and explicit instructions where necessary; improved manuals increase interrater reliability (eg, adapted Fugl-Meyer manual led to excellent ICCs for motor scores).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of number of trials and averaging on reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Influence of repeated measurements and averaging on improving reliability metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple repeated registrations (eg, 2–3 trials) typically yield higher ICCs than single-trial measurements; specify recommended number of repetitions for acceptable reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modification of classification instruments to improve reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Altering or removing unreliable elements of a grading/classification system to improve interrater agreement (eg, removing high intensity zones (HIZ) from Tufts classification).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform sensitivity analyses to identify poorly reproducible elements; consider simplifying systems for routine clinical use while preserving detail for research (eg, Paley system easier clinically; KLGS preferred for research).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tool-specific measurement-property reporting (area/length vs depth/volume)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognition that different measurement dimensions may have different reliability (eg, wound area/length very reliable; depth/volume less reliable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report ICCs separately for each measurement dimension (length, width, area, depth, volume) and discuss which metrics are robust enough for clinical decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of interobserver variability in scoring systems (peer review and audit contexts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate reproducibility of scoring systems used for peer review or quality audits (eg, RADPEER, Cleareview, web-based lecture ratings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report kappa or ICC results; low interobserver correlation (eg, κ ≈ 0.1–0.3) indicates poor reproducibility and suggests need to evaluate or replace the peer review instrument or process.
